title: Human-AI Collaboration in Biomedicine
audience: Basic science learners reflecting on human-AI collaboration tools in research settings
objectives: Identify human-AI collaboration tools currently used in labs or professional organizations.
Evaluate benefits, drawbacks, and data-management practices for those tools.
Analyze whether an AI transcription tool should be used after hallucination, tone distortion, accent-bias, and metadata privacy issues are found.
Practice balancing workflow benefits against research integrity, fairness, and privacy risks.

sections.name: Question 1
sections.purpose: Inventory current human-AI collaboration tools and governance practices.
sections.how_to_use: List tools used in your research setting, explain how they are used, note benefits and drawbacks, and describe how outputs/data are managed.

sections.name: Question 2
sections.purpose: Analyze a flawed AI transcription tool in qualitative public-health research.
sections.how_to_use: Consider hallucinated content, mischaracterized tone, accent-related errors, metadata privacy, and whether safeguards or rejection are appropriate.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through Question 1 first, then the transcription case.
For basic science users, emphasize research integrity, consent, privacy, data provenance, accent bias, and human review.
Help learners give a concrete recommendation, not just list pros and cons.
